svg.title: Blind ring: NHL '94 and NHL '95
svg.text: Through the legs: where a puck on the ice can pass through the goalie (Genesis)
Seen from above, to scale. Each goalie faces down the page, his net behind him at the top. Only a puck on the ice (height 5 or less, not rising) is affected.
NHL '94: butterfly save
frame 480
NHL '95: kick / butterfly save to his left
frame 634; dots measured in the game
NHL '95: standing ready
frame 610; dots measured in the game
A blind ring, 8-14 units from the stick blade.
The blade is 9 units to his side, so the ring
crosses his middle. Only a thin sliver of his
body is checked in front of it.
A blind square, 14 units each way from the blade
(a distance bug makes it square, not round). The
blade is 10 units to his side, so the square covers
his middle back to the goal line. About 7 units
of his body are still checked in front of it.
Standing, his body is never checked: all of it
lies inside the blind square. Only the stick,
within 8 units of the blade, can stop the puck.
Body: a puck here hits him. Reach by Agility: NHL '94 12-15 (13 here), NHL '95 14-19 (18 here). Dashed: never checked
Stick: within 8 units of the blade (white dot) the stick plays the puck
Blind area: nothing is checked here, so the puck passes through him. NHL '94: a ring. NHL '95: a square
Measured in NHL '95: a puck placed here on the ice passed untouched
Red line: the goal line. Under the shapes, each game's own sprite for that frame. Lifted shots skip these checks and are saved by his body as usual, which is why through-the-legs goals are rare.
NHL '95's other poses (gloves, skating) have blind areas too; its dive has none. NOSE4Web's five-hole fix for NHL '95 makes the game check his body there, closing nearly all of them.
